analysis.title: Showdowns
key_insights: Week ahead is framed as a series of showdowns: US midterms on Tuesday, a possible resumption of the US war against Iran afterwards, the RBA and BoE rate decisions, and US payrolls on Friday.
Prediction markets favour the Democrats overwhelmingly to take the House and, less assuredly, the Senate in the US midterms.

Risk is heightened that President Trump resumes the war against Iran after the midterms. Both sides say the gloves will be off and the target list expanded. Iranian figures say there are no geographical limitations to retaliation, which could include European countries assisting the US, and cyberattacks are considered likely.

Active Brent crude futures settled 2.4% higher on Friday and opened slightly softer Monday. US equities fell sharply Friday, with the Nasdaq composite seeing particularly heavy declines. Asian stocks are mixed Monday. Treasury yields were steady, while most European sovereign yields (except France, Italy and Greece) finished lower.
Fitch placed France's credit rating on negative outlook.

Axios reports Netanyahu is urging Trump to strike immediately after the midterms, while behind-the-scenes talks continue on a deal. Trump wants concessions on Iran's nuclear program and Iran is unlikely to give them. Iran's foreign minister says a plan to re-open Hormuz within two days is being explored, but without progress on the nuclear issue the US is unlikely to give up its leverage over Iranian oil flows.

Israel is in political deadlock after an indecisive election in which Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority. The opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot cannot govern in its own right and faces difficult deals with Arab parties or ultra-orthodox parties. President Herzog has invited both leaders to talks Wednesday, which the report sees as unlikely to produce a unity government. Fresh elections are a possible outcome.
Poland faces a constitutional crisis after Tusk's government deployed troops to secure the constitutional court building. President Nawrocki turned his jet around to return to Warsaw.

China's Central Committee plenary had its lowest attendance since the Mao era, with up to a quarter of members from the start of the term absent after purges. The seven-seat Central Military Commission has only two serving members, Xi and Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin. Analysts question China's preparedness to fight a war over Taiwan in the near term.

New Zealand holds a general election this weekend. Prediction markets favour the National, ACT and New Zealand First coalition for a second term. The RBNZ's surprise decision to hold the OCR at 2.75% last week may help the incumbents.

The RBA meets Tuesday and is widely tipped, including by the author, to raise rates 25bp to 4.85%, the fifth hike this year. RBA Deputy Governor Hauser said the inflation outlook has become materially worse.
The BoE decides Thursday, with a 25bp hike to 4% favoured by the Bloomberg survey and by RaboResearch's Stefan Koopman.
US non-farm payrolls on Friday are expected at +65,000 for October, with unemployment steady at 4.2%.
Eurozone October flash CPI on Wednesday is expected to show headline inflation rising to 4% with core at 2.5%.

Favoured by the Bloomberg survey and by RaboResearch's Stefan Koopman.
Expected October payroll gain, the key US data point on Friday.
Headline inflation expected to rise to 4%.

risk_factors: Resumption of US war with Iran after the midterms, with expanded targets and retaliation that could reach Europe and include cyberattacks.
Continued closure or restriction of the Strait of Hormuz and US leverage over Iranian oil flows.
Worsening inflation outlook in Australia, which could worsen further with Middle East events.
French sovereign credit risk after the Fitch negative outlook.
Reduced Chinese military leadership capacity and questions over Taiwan readiness.
geopolitical: Possible resumption of the US-Israel war against Iran after the US midterms, with both sides saying targets will expand.
Iran says there are no geographical limitations to retaliation, which may include European countries assisting the US, and cyberattacks.
Iran's foreign minister says a plan to re-open the Strait of Hormuz within two days is being explored.
Behind-the-scenes US-Iran negotiations over Iran's nuclear program.
Israeli political deadlock after an indecisive election, with Herzog inviting Netanyahu and Eisenkot to talks Wednesday.
Poland's constitutional court crisis between the Tusk government and President Nawrocki.
Purges in China's Central Committee and Central Military Commission, with analysts questioning near-term Taiwan war readiness.
New Zealand general election this weekend.
Senator Chris Murphy was hospitalised after an apparent stroke, after calling the administration's attack plans on Iran insane.

tension_points.bull_case: Behind-the-scenes negotiations are underway to reach a deal that avoids war, and Iran's foreign minister says a plan to re-open Hormuz within two days is being explored.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump wants nuclear concessions Iran will not give, Netanyahu is urging an immediate strike after the midterms, and both sides say targets will expand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Progress on Iran's nuclear program in the negotiations would reduce the chance of war. The report names the US midterms on Tuesday as the trigger point after which strikes may resume.

theme_stances.key_argument: Without progress on the nuclear issue it seems unlikely that the US would give up its leverage over Iranian oil flows.
theme_stances.evidence: heightened risk that President Trump will make good on his hints to resume the war

theme_stances.evidence: widely tipped to deliver another 25bp rate rise
